title: Spare moves and knight parity

D0.outcome: Explains spare moves (tempo reserves) in endings and knight parity: a knight reaches a given square only in an odd or only in an even number of moves.

D1.outcome: Counts the spare moves for both sides in a locked pawn ending and says who must give way.

D2.outcome: In unlabeled positions, uses knight parity to decide whether a knight can lose a move while a bishop can, and decides when to keep a pawn move in reserve.

D3.outcome: Predicts the result of a mutual-zugzwang ending from the count and verifies it by the tablebase check.

conditions: A knight cannot lose a move because of its parity, whereas a bishop can.
contrasts: With pieces on the board such positions are infrequent, so the count rarely applies.
An open position where pieces can pass the move.
